claim: As of July 1, 2025, the United States had 331,449,281 residents.
note: Constructed date substitution. The fixture paraphrases Census QuickFacts and preserves both published values.

sources.title: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts: United States
sources.text: The 2020 Census counted 331,449,281 U.S. residents on April 1, 2020. For July 1, 2025, the Census Bureau estimates 341,784,857 U.S. residents.

claim: North America had about 340.1 million residents on July 1, 2024.
note: Constructed geographic overgeneralization. The fixture paraphrases the national estimate, which does not enumerate the continent.

sources.title: U.S. Census Bureau: New 2024 Population Estimates
sources.text: On July 1, 2024, the United States population was estimated at 340.1 million, compared with 336.8 million as of July 1, 2023. These are U.S. national population estimates.

claim: Yellowstone recreation visits increased by 44% from 2023 to 2024.
note: Constructed baseline swap. The fixture paraphrases the Park Facts figures and the agency's description of the flood year.

sources.title: National Park Service: Yellowstone Park Facts
sources.text: Yellowstone counted 4,744,353 visits in 2024 and 4,501,382 visits in 2023. NPS compared 2024 to 2022 for its reported 44% increase. Floods interrupted access to parts of Yellowstone in 2022.

claim: Yellowstone's 44% increase in recreation visits from 2022 to 2024 proves that a new marketing campaign caused the increase.
note: Constructed causal claim. The visitation numbers and flood disruption in the paraphrased fixture are real. No causal conclusion about marketing follows from them.

sources.title: National Park Service: Yellowstone Park Facts
sources.text: Yellowstone had approximately 4.74 million recreation visits in 2024, a 44% increase relative to 2022. Flood damage in 2022 limited public access to parts of the park.

claim: Two official NPS reports disagree on Yellowstone's 2024 recreation visit total: one reported 4,744,353 and the other reported 2,324,734.
note: Constructed disagreement based on real NPS figures. The fixtures paraphrase the park-wide and state-level tables. The second figure is a Wyoming allocation, so the two reports are not describing the same scope.

sources.title: National Park Service: Yellowstone Park Facts
sources.text: The annual visitation figures for Yellowstone National Park list 4,744,353 recreation visits for 2024.

sources.title: National Park Service: Statistical Abstract 2024, figures by state
sources.text: The state-level recreation table lists 2,324,734 Yellowstone National Park recreation visits under Wyoming for 2024. This table groups figures by state; the park spans Wyoming, Montana and Idaho.

claim: About 1.3% of all water on Earth is freshwater in lakes and rivers at the surface.
note: Constructed denominator substitution. The fixture paraphrases the USGS graphic explanation. About 1.3% is a share of freshwater, itself about 2.5% of all water.

sources.title: USGS Water Science School: Where is Earth's Water?
sources.text: USGS estimates that freshwater makes up 2.5% of all Earth's water. Surface water such as lakes and rivers represents about 1.3% of freshwater.

claim: NASA's dates for Armstrong's first step conflict because one record says July 20, 1969 and another says July 21, 1969.
note: Constructed apparent disagreement. Both excerpts paraphrase NASA records. Even the NASA timeline assigns different dates to the same instant because it presents several time standards.

sources.title: NASA History: Apollo 11 Record of Lunar Events
sources.text: The same Armstrong-on-lunar-surface event appears at 02:56:15 GMT on July 21, 1969 and at 21:56:15 Eastern Standard Time on July 20, 1969 in the NASA table.

sources.title: NASA Apollo Lunar Surface Journal: One Small Step
sources.text: The surface journal identifies Armstrong's first step by mission elapsed time, about 109 hours and 24 minutes after launch. Its step record describes the same event as the record of lunar events.

claim: NASA reports conflicting lengths of time from one new Moon to the next: 27.3 days and 29.5 days.
note: Constructed apparent disagreement. These paraphrased primary materials measure different events: an orbit around Earth and a return to the same visible lunar phase.

sources.title: NASA Glenn Research Center: Moon
sources.text: The Moon makes a complete orbit around Earth in 27.3 days. This is an orbital revolution around Earth.

sources.title: NASA Science: Moon Phases
sources.text: A full sequence of lunar phases takes about 29.5 days from new Moon to new Moon. The Moon goes around Earth in about 27.3 days, so the phase cycle takes longer than an orbital revolution.

claim: The Moon is always 238,855 miles away from Earth.
note: Constructed average-to-constant substitution. The first fixture is a brief exact extract. The second is a paraphrase of NASA's explanation of lunar distance.

sources.title: NASA Science: Moon Facts
sources.text: The Moon is an average of 238,855 miles (384,400 kilometers) away.

sources.title: NASA Space Place: How Far Away Is the Moon?
sources.text: The Moon's distance changes because its orbit is not circular. The distance is about 225,309 miles at the closest point and 251,903 miles at the farthest point.

claim: NASA voted to reclassify Pluto as a dwarf planet in 2006.

sources.title: International Astronomical Union: 2006 General Assembly resolution votes
sources.text: In 2006, members of the International Astronomical Union voted on the definitions of planet and dwarf planet at the IAU General Assembly. The adopted resolution classified Pluto as a dwarf planet.

claim: Under the Gregorian calendar, 2000 was a leap year, but 1900 was not.

sources.title: U.S. Naval Observatory: Leap Years
sources.text: Under Gregorian rules, years divisible by 4 are leap years except for century years not divisible by 400. This makes 2000 a leap year and 1900 a common year.
